brief: A man's oxblood silk pocket square, crumpled and pooled on a slab of black Marquina marble, cropped so its folds spill off two edges. Build it in watercolour: many transparent glazes of alizarin, burnt sienna and a whisper of ultramarine in the troughs. Leave paper bare where the sheen catches, so each ridge carries a thin, almost white highlight that slides into wine-dark shadow within a hair's width. Deep fold interiors get soft charcoal-like mass for velvety black. The marble stays cool and matte, threaded with fine grey pencil veins. The mood is hushed, expensive and slightly dishevelled.

A hyperreal bowl of borscht seen from a steep three-quarter angle. Its beet-crimson surface shimmers with oily droplets, and a glossy spoonful of sour cream is swirling into pink. The bowl is Khokhloma lacquerware: a jet-black ground scrolled with vermilion berries and gilded curling grasses, all drawn with a fine gold-ink pen and loose flicked strokes. Render the lacquer with deep, liquid reflections, with a window highlight stretched across its curve in thin white marker. Dark rye crumbs and a sprig of dill sit on a black lacquered tray. The palette is strictly black, vermilion, cinnabar, gold and soup-red. The feeling is warm, ceremonial and wintry.

A goldfinch clinging to a dried thistle head, painted in the logic of pysanky wax resist. Colour is built in strict dye-bath order: paper white, then lemon yellow, then marigold orange, then cochineal red, and finally a glossy blue-black ground. Lighter colours survive only where they were "waxed" first, so every feather barb, eye glint and thistle filament is a reserved hairline of pale colour cutting through darker layers. The bird is hyperreal in plumage and anatomy, but every edge has the crisp, slightly beaded quality of a stylus-drawn wax line. The surface feels lacquered and jewel-dark, like a decorated egg shell.

A wide, low-angle view of a cheap motel room at night, lit only by a bedside lamp with a pleated shade and the orange glow of a bathroom doorway. Deep transparent watercolour glazes in burnt umber, raw sienna and amber build the warm falloff, and the corners sink into brownish violet murk. A floral polyester bedspread, an ashtray, a half-unpacked duffel and a TV's dead grey screen are each rendered with forensic detail inside the pools of light. Soft graphite carries the shadows' grain. The mood is lonely and cinematic, with heavy gradients and no hard edges except where the lampshade throws its sharp ring onto the wall.

An extreme horizontal crop of a closed eye, stretched like a spectrometer readout across a long thin frame. The eyeshadow is blended as a continuous spectral gradient, running from violet at the inner corner through blue, green and yellow to deep red at the outer edge. The lashes and fine creases fall as crisp vertical dark lines of varying weight, so they read exactly like absorption lines against the spectrum. Skin pores, tiny shimmer particles and a single stray lash are rendered precisely with watercolour and fine pencil. Above and below runs a thin graphite wavelength scale with tick marks. The image is cool, precise and quietly intimate.

A ruby grapefruit half seen dead-on from above, its segments treated as an Art Deco sunburst. Each wedge of glistening pulp is a crisp radiating panel, and the rays continue outward past the rind into a lacquered black ground as thin metallic-gold marker lines. The fruit itself is hyperreal: individual juice vesicles, wet specular glints and a translucent membrane rendered in layered watercolour glazes of rose madder, coral and blush. The pith reads as a creamy ring. Strict bilateral symmetry gives the image the poise of a cinema-foyer emblem, but the dripping juice at one edge breaks the geometry just enough.

A roast chicken on a carving board, depicted as a marquetry panel of cut wood veneers. Every area is a discrete flat shape with its own directional grain: honey maple for the breast, scorched walnut for crisp skin, pale sycamore for the platter, rosewood for drippings. Fine flowing lines carry the grain within each piece, and hair-thin dark joins separate them. Shading comes from sand-scorched edges, darkened as if dipped in hot sand, so the bird reads as fully three-dimensional and glistening. A satin varnish glow sits over the whole. It is craftsmanly, warm and slyly trompe-l'oeil.

Twelve pieces of produce arranged in a perfect ring on a pale grey board, ordered like a theory chart's hue wheel. The ring runs from red chilli to tangerine, banana, lime, cucumber, savoy cabbage, red cabbage, aubergine, beetroot and radicchio. Each is rendered in exacting watercolour realism, with cast shadows tinted in its complementary hue. Fine ruled pen lines connect opposite pairs across the centre, and small hand-lettered labels in graphite name primaries, secondaries and tertiaries. Flat marker swatches sit beside each item like a test chart. The feel is didactic, bright and orderly, a classroom diagram made edible.

A mid-century motel pool is shot from above at a steep angle. A sunburnt man in a straw hat sleeps on a striped lounger, one arm trailing toward turquoise water. The palette has the punchy, dense saturation of a slide: candy-apple red stripes, cyan pool and deep inky shadows. The skin glows warm salmon with peeling detail. Watercolour is glazed in rich layers, with crisp pencil detail on the woven plastic straps and the ripple caustics on the pool floor. A thin cardboard slide-mount border frames the scene, with a faint handwritten date. It is nostalgic, sharp and sun-struck.

Three cut lemon halves resting on a crumpled cotton cloth, rendered almost entirely in rows of short, evenly spaced pen dashes that imitate kantha running stitch. The dashes follow every contour like quilting lines: concentric arcs across the pulp, radial lines along each segment wall, rippling parallel rows through the cloth's folds. Density of stitching builds the form. Thread colours are cadmium lemon, saffron, leaf green, faded madder pink and indigo, laid on a pale unbleached-cotton ground with a faint watercolour tint. Read up close, it is pure stitched rhythm. From a step back it resolves into wet, glistening citrus with juice beads and pith fibres. The feel is patient, homely and luminous.

A heap of split jackfruit on a woven mat, rendered in the manner of kalamkari hand-painted cotton. Confident, slightly swelling outlines in iron black are drawn as if with a bamboo pen. Fills are natural-dye washes: turmeric yellow for the bulbs, madder red and alizarin for the mat, indigo for shadow, and myrobalan olive for the spiky rind. The rendering is hyperreal: sticky latex threads, glossy fleshy pods and the geometric knobbed skin. Tone builds through layered translucent dye rather than blending, on a warm ecru cotton ground with faint bleed at the edges. The feeling is lush, abundant and handmade.

A sleeping greyhound curled nose-to-tail on a bare floor, seen from slightly above. It is rendered as though fired from unglazed earthenware. The palette stays strictly within clay: raw sienna, burnt sienna, iron-oxide red, umber and chalky slip white. Smudged charcoal mass and dry, granular watercolour create a matte, powdery surface without a single wet highlight, and the ribs, folded ears and paw pads are modelled through soft directional light. Faint hairline cracks and kiln-mottled colour shifts ripple across the flanks without hiding the realism of fur and skin. It is warm and tactile, like a sculpture you could knock on.

Looking straight up at a ceiling crowded with dozens of matte latex balloons pressed together after a party. Their rounded undersides hang down in heavy pendulous lobes, like a mammatus cloud base. Soft charcoal and smudged graphite model each bulge, glazed with bruised mauve, dusty plum and stormy slate, and a sickly warm amber catches the lowest curves from an unseen lamp. Curling ribbons dangle down as fine pen lines. Wrinkled knots, faint latex sheen and a fallen streamer are rendered precisely. The overall feeling is oppressive and strange, festive debris turned into a brooding sky.

A motorcycle helmet seen in tight three-quarter view, printed as if pulled through limited screens. The smoked visor holds a perfectly rendered reflection of a desert highway and telephone poles. Colour comes as flat, opaque marker-like layers of fluorescent orange, slate blue, warm black and bone. Each layer is slightly misregistered so thin slivers of paper show at the edges. Spray grit stands in for halftone texture in the gradients, coarse in the shadows and fading to bare paper in the highlights. Scuffs and stickers on the shell are hyperreal, but the ink-layer logic flattens space into stacked, graphic planes.

An open industrial dryer drum in a laundromat, with towels tumbling out onto the floor, seen through a thermal camera. Heat is the only light source. The coolest areas are deep indigo and violet, warming through magenta, scarlet and orange to near-white yellow at the hot core of the drum. Smooth spray gradients carry the thermal bloom, and markers give crisp boundaries where cold metal meets hot cotton. Terry loops, folds and the drum's perforations stay hyperreal in form despite the false colour. A small temperature scale bar and crosshair overlay sit in one corner. It feels clinical and oddly cosy.

A single scuffed leather motorcycle boot lying on its side, done as a two-stone lithograph. The key stone is a warm lamp-black built from reticulated tusche washes that crackle and pool into lizard-skin patterns across the creased leather. Over it, grainy crayon passages give the gritty tooth of stone. A second stone adds one flat tint of muted olive ochre, slightly off-register so a sliver of paper shows along one edge. Highlights are scraped-back paper white on the toe cap and buckle. The boot fills the frame at a low angle, and every scratch and salt stain is described. The mood is heavy, tactile and print-shop dirty.

A red cabbage sliced cleanly in half and shown face-on, filling the frame edge to edge like a cracked geode. It is built from many transparent watercolour glazes: a deep violet-black rind, then pulsing bands of magenta, amethyst and milky lavender. Pale veins branch inward like crystal seams toward a dense, folded core. A crisp graphite line holds each lamella. The sheen on the wet cut face is reserved as bare paper. A faint dew of moisture beads along the outer leaves. There is no background, only the cross-section, cool and mineral, with layered saturation that rewards close looking.

A horizontal sequence of frames in the manner of an early motion study. A grey striped cat twists in mid-fall, frame by frame, from upside-down to feet-first. It is drawn in graphite on warm grey paper. Behind each frame sits a ruled grid of measurement lines, slightly smudged. Each pose is hyperreal: separated fur, splayed toes, ears flattened. Faint ghosting trails between the frames suggest the exposure. The tonal range is narrow and silvery, the frame edges slightly irregular, like old plates. The feeling is scientific yet comic, a record of an impossible twist.

A tall ribbed glass of layered iced coffee seen from a dramatically low angle, so it rises like a setback tower against a jade-black night sky. Ice cubes stack like stepped terraces, and the cream layer forms a pale spandrel band. The composition is strictly bilaterally symmetrical, with fluted condensation streaks running vertically like pilasters. Dense marker fills of espresso brown, ivory and jade carry the tones, accented with fine metallic-gold pen hatching along every rim and highlight. Condensation beads are meticulously rendered. The mood is glamorous, rigid and vertical.

Ultra-shallow focus on a tabby cat's muzzle in profile. Only the whisker pads, a few whiskers and the wet edge of the nose are tack-sharp, drawn in fine pen and pencil. Everything else melts. The ear, the window and a sunny kitchen dissolve into large overlapping watercolour discs of apricot, sage and butter-cream. They are wet-in-wet, with soft blooms and hard dried rims, like real lens aberration. The cat's fur grades from crisp individual hairs to diffuse washes. The light is honest daylight, warm and domestic, and the composition is pushed off-centre so that blur dominates.
